questions.q: What core problem does Single Sign-On solve?
options: It replaces the need for profiles and permission sets
It lets one authentication event be trusted by multiple systems, instead of each system maintaining its own password database
It makes Salesforce data encrypted at rest
It eliminates the need for session timeouts
questions.explain: SSO means a user authenticates once with a single system, and other systems trust that authentication event rather than asking for separate credentials.

questions.q: In Salesforce Setup, where is federated SAML authentication configured?
options: Session Settings
Single Sign-On Settings
App Manager
Login IP Ranges
questions.explain: Single Sign-On Settings is the Setup page where SAML is enabled, the IdP certificate is uploaded, and SAML SSO configuration records are defined.

questions.q: A user clicks an app tile on their company's Okta dashboard and lands directly in Salesforce, authenticated, with no redirect from Salesforce itself. What pattern is this?
options: SP-initiated SSO
IdP-initiated SSO
Delegated authentication
Just-in-time provisioning
questions.explain: Because the flow started at the identity provider's own portal and the IdP proactively sent the assertion, this is IdP-initiated SSO.

questions.q: If two users have identical profiles and permission sets, but one logs in via SSO and the other with a Salesforce username/password, what's true about what each user can do?
options: The SSO user automatically gets more access
The password user automatically gets more access
They can do exactly the same things, since authorization doesn't depend on the login method
Neither user can do anything until an admin manually syncs permissions
questions.explain: SSO changes how a user authenticates, not what they're authorized to do. Identical profiles and permission sets mean identical access, regardless of login method.

questions.q: What is the Identity Provider Certificate field on the Single Sign-On Settings page used for?
options: It stores the user's password hash
It's the cryptographic trust anchor Salesforce uses to validate the IdP's signed assertions
It defines which profiles can use SSO
It sets the session timeout duration
questions.explain: Salesforce validates every incoming SAML assertion's signature against the uploaded IdP certificate before trusting it and establishing a session.
